question: Which ZIP64 emission policy should ZIP export use when output cannot be prepared in memory or goes to a non-seekable sink (R1 §8.3 Tier 3; §21 item 14): whole-archive in-memory AsNeeded (zip/portable-v1), per-entry buffering, temp-file staging, an Always-ZIP64 streaming profile with data descriptors, Never-ZIP64 with pre-write refusal, fail-late AsNeeded, or refusing large non-seekable ZIP output?
archetypal_objective: Large releases must be exportable to ZIP files and pipes without unbounded memory, silent mid-stream failure or bytes that differ from a frozen profile, while remaining readable by mainstream ZIP readers and registry validators. The repo avoids the fork today only by preparing every byte in memory first.
hard_constraints: docs/zip-export-v1.md L22-29: zip/portable-v1 frozen; ZIP64 exactly when a size, offset or EOCD field needs its sentinel; data descriptors never emitted
docs/legacy-export-v1.md L62-64: binary stdout prepared completely before the first byte
Frozen export profiles untouched: a different byte policy needs a new profile id
I13 (export losses and refusals declared, never silent)
R1 §8.3 L600: more than 65,535 entries require ZIP64

candidate_set.description: Prepare the whole ZIP in memory, then write; exact local headers, ZIP64 only where a sentinel is needed, no data descriptors (export.rs:880-900, 1098-1140); memory scales with archive size
Stream entry by entry to any sink, buffering one entry's encoded payload so sizes and CRC are known before its header; bytes identical to zip/portable-v1; memory bounded by the largest encoded entry
Write zip/portable-v1 to a seekable temporary file, then copy to the sink; bounded RAM, one archive of temporary disk

New streaming profile writing ZIP64 extras for every entry plus data descriptors (Commons Compress Always, Java and Go streaming writers); no buffering, different bytes, rejected by PyPI-style validators that refuse descriptors
Emit classic ZIP only and refuse, before writing, any archive with members or offsets at 4 GiB or more than 65,535 entries
Commons Compress default: choose ZIP64 per entry from what is known and fail mid-stream when an entry turns out to need it, leaving partial output on a pipe
Require a seekable destination for ZIP exports above a declared size or entry threshold; small exports keep in-memory preparation

required_evidence: Peak memory, temporary disk and wall time for multi-GiB and >65,535-entry ZIP exports to files and pipes under each candidate
Byte identity of per-entry-buffered and temp-staged output with zip/portable-v1 vectors

Reader acceptance of Always-ZIP64 plus data-descriptor output (Info-ZIP unzip, Python zipfile, Java ZipFile and ZipInputStream, Go archive/zip, .NET, 7-Zip, Windows Explorer, PyPI warehouse validate_zipfile)
Demand for ZIP export to non-seekable sinks in release and CI workflows

requirement_or_question: Streaming ZIP read may be offered as policy, but its results must be labelled untrusted, and STORED entries whose sizes are deferred to a data descriptor must be refused as unresolvable in a stream. Entrybound imports only from a complete in-memory source via the central directory; no local-header streaming import mode exists.
